newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. advanced Q2 GDP up 2.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. advanced Q2 GDP up 2.2 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Commerce Department said Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rose 2.2 percent in the second quarter compared to a revised 4.9 percent in the first quarter.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 1.9-percent rise in second quarter GDP.

WAYNE AYERS, CHIEF ECONOMIST, BANK OF BOSTON: "In terms of the major contours it came in pretty much as expected. The second quarter was a touch above the consensus but we had a fairly substantial revision to the first quarter."

"If you look at both quarters together, I think it's probably still fair to say that the first quarter overstated the strength of the economy and the second quarter number, even though it came in higher than expectations, probably overstated the weakness.

"But net/net, the figures, both for the quarter and first half (of the year) continue to portray an economy that is moving ahead at a healthy pace and a pace that is accompanied by virtually no sign of inflationary pressures, current or potential."

ASTRID ADOLFSON, FIRST VICE PRESIDENT AND AN ECONOMIST, MCM MONEYWATCH: "It was in line with what we were looking for. Inventories were up a little bit and some of the components were a little softer. It shows a slight slowdown but not as much as people were looking at. It's a slight pause coming off of a very decent quarterly pace."
CHERYL KATZ, SENIOR ECONOMIST, MERRILL LYNCH: "Growth came in higher than expectations and the price component came in a little bit lower. You can't really get much better than that sort of mix.
"Things look very favorable. Inflation pressures remain extremely muted and economic growth was strong.
"With this sort of mix I think the Fed will remain on hold for the rest of this year. This is a continuation of a sort of nirvana state for the U.S. economy."

RAYMOND WORSECK, CHIEF ECONOMIST AT A.G. EDWARDS AND SONS INC: "Well some mish and some mash and kind of a wash. (It showed a) downward revision in the first quarter growth and higher than expected second quarter growth, so that is an offset of sorts, and a very low deflator number, which is positive for bonds.
"But no big story there anywhere. A little bit below in some a little above in others but the revision in the first quarter kind of takes the fun out of the better than expected second quarter."
